correctness.rationale: Gupta Proposition 2.4 was independently inspected directly, including its derivation from the squared-distance supporting inequality and normal-modulus bound. It gives the quantitative collar loss \(C_0\delta^2(\rho(A\delta)^2+2\tau_\delta/\delta^2)^2\) for \(\rho(r)=\sup_{0<t\le r}\omega_\nu(t)/\sqrt t\); its intermediate bounds remain valid for bounded nonzero \(\rho\), since no limiting zero is used until the strict-positive conclusion. With \(\tau_\delta=\delta^3\), the loss is \(C_0\delta^2(\rho(A\delta)^2+2\delta)^2\). The positive quadratic perturbation in Gupta Proposition 2.5 via Edigarian Lemma 2.4 adds \(c\delta^2/(1+R^2)\). By definition of limsup, \(\rho(A\delta)\to\Lambda_\nu\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), so the stated strict fourth-power threshold leaves a uniformly positive \(\delta^2\)-order margin. Gupta proves the collar inclusion and regularized level-set completion from this margin and \(\tau_\delta/\delta\to0\); its final step cites Edigarian for nesting/exhaustion and does not use vanishing of \(\rho\) elsewhere. Consequently small positive critical modulus can be admitted; the threshold is sufficient, not sharp.
residual_risks: The full Edigarian proof could not be retrieved in this run; the exact quadratic-perturbation lemma was cross-checked where Gupta applies and quotes it.

final_claim:
For a bounded \(\mathbb C\)-convex \(C^1\) domain \(D\subset\mathbb C^n\), \(n\ge2\), with outward normal modulus \(\omega_
u(t)\) and \(\Lambda_
u=\limsup_{t\downarrow0}\omega_
u(t)/\sqrt t\), fix a containing radius \(R\), \(0<c<1/[20(1+R^2)]\), and the constant \(C_0\) in the Gupta smoothing defect inequality. If \(\Lambda_
u<(c/[C_0(1+R^2)])^{1/4}\), then \(D\) admits an increasing exhaustion by smooth bounded strongly linearly convex domains, with the resulting Lempert and infinitesimal-metric equalities. In particular sufficiently small \(C^{0,1/2}\) seminorm of the normal suffices even without little-Hölder decay.
limitations: Explicit threshold depends on regularization constant and containing radius and is not optimal or intrinsic.
Does not address arbitrary large critical Hölder normal seminorms; institutional access to full Edigarian text was blocked.
